(c) The correct match of given cities with their related rivers is as follows : (City) (River) Rotterdam - Rhine Paris - Seine Budapest - Danube Washington - Potomac Landforms by River *In rivers, erosion, transportation and deposition go on simultaneously from the point of its origin to the point where it meets the sea. This process leads to the formation of diﬀ erent terrestrial relief features. Some of them are as follows- Gorge - It is a deep narrow section of river valley usually with near vertical rock walls, more generally a narrow valley between hills and mountains. Gorges are formed as a result of continued erosion of mountainous terrain by a river. For Ex: Chisapani Gorge in Nepal, which is formed by river Karnali. Karnali is the longest river in Nepal (507 km). It is due to the high velocity of the river that it creates a lot of Gorges. Canyon- Canyons are the more eroded version of Gorges. Grand Canyon is located in Arizona (US). It is a steep-sided canyon carved by river Colorado. The canyon is 446 km long, 4 to 24 km wide and 1.6 km deep. V-shaped Valley- V-shaped valleys are formed by erosion. The majority of the rivers of the world carry on two processes simultaneously i.e. vertical and horizontal erosion respectively. These rivers create V-shaped valleys. Waterfalls- It is a stream that falls from a height. Waterfalls are often the sites of the greatest concentration of energy dissipation along the course of a stream. Meanders- As water ﬂ owing under gravity seldom ﬂ ows straight for any long distance, a winding course soon appears. The irregularities of the ground force the river to swing in loops, forming meanders. Alluvial Cones - Also called Alluvial fan, is a cone-shaped deposit of sediments built by a stream where it merges into a broad valley or plain. Delta- When the river reaches a sea, the ﬁ ne materials it has not yet dropped are deposited at its mouth, forming a fan-shaped alluvial area called Delta. This alluvial tract is, in fact, a seaward extension of the ﬂ ood plains. Deltas diﬀ er much in size, shape, growth and importance. A number of factors such as the rate of sedimentation the depth of the river, the sea bed, the character of tides, currents and waves greatly inﬂ uence the eventual formation of Deltas.
